The *hogy*-clause names the condition; a comma stands before *azzal* and before *hogy*.

old: Deontic treaty predicates (*köteles tiszteletben tartani* [is obliged to respect], *vállalja, hogy szavatolja* [undertakes to guarantee], *kötelezettséget ró a tagállamokra* [imposes an obligation on member states], *kötelességévé teszi* [makes it its duty]) define legal requirements in multilateral pacts.
new: You know *köteles* from B1 Unit 10. Treaty language adds *kötelezettséget vállal* (takes on an obligation), *kötelezettséget ró valakire* (imposes an obligation on someone) and *vállalja, hogy* (undertakes to). A *vállal* clause names who takes the duty on; a *ró* clause names who must carry it.

old: Discourse summation particles (*végeredményben* [in the final analysis / ultimately], *summázva* [summarizing], *összességében nézve* [looking at it on the whole], *mindent egybevetve* [taking everything together]) draw rigorous overarching conclusions in analytical essays.
new: You know metaphor from C1 Unit 6: a word is used figuratively to say something about a thing. Writers on Central Europe use three images: *híd* (a bridge between East and West), *kompország* (a 'ferry country', a land that shuttles between two shores) and *ütközőállam* (a buffer state between two power blocs).
